es: Identificar la causa, el supuesto cultural y la mejor reacción en relatos de malentendidos entre culturas.

usesVocabulary: give the benefit of the doubt

vocabulary.en: give the benefit of the doubt
vocabulary.es: conceder el beneficio de la duda

teaching.en: Many visitors assume that dinner is at nine, a hidden assumption that surprises a host family eating at six.
teaching.es: Muchos visitantes suponen que la cena es a las nueve, un supuesto oculto que sorprende a una familia anfitriona que cena a las seis.
teaching.explanationEs: Assume = suponer: creemos algo sin haberlo preguntado.
segments: Many visitors assume that dinner is at nine, a hidden
assumption that surprises a host family eating at six.
teaching.audioText: Many visitors assume that dinner is at nine, a hidden assumption that surprises a host family eating at six.

teaching.en: Tom felt embarrassed because nobody had told him about the custom of bringing a small gift.
teaching.es: Tom se sintió avergonzado porque nadie le había hablado de la costumbre de llevar un pequeño regalo.
teaching.explanationEs: Embarrassed describe cómo se siente la persona; embarrassing describe la situación.
segments: Tom felt embarrassed because nobody had told him
about the custom of bringing a small gift.

teaching.en: The misunderstanding began when Mia took “We will see” as a yes, while her host meant it as a polite no.
teaching.es: El malentendido empezó cuando Mia tomó «Ya veremos» como un sí, mientras que su anfitrión lo decía como un no cortés.
teaching.explanationEs: El supuesto de Mia no coincidía con el del anfitrión.
segments: The misunderstanding began when Mia took “We will see” as a
yes, while her host meant it as a polite no.
teaching.audioText: The misunderstanding began when Mia took “We will see” as a yes, while her host meant it as a polite no.

teaching.en: In some families silence is not rude; a guest who stays quiet may come across as thoughtful rather than unfriendly.
teaching.es: En algunas familias el silencio no es de mala educación; un invitado que calla puede parecer reflexivo y no antipático.
teaching.explanationEs: Lo que parece maleducado en una cultura puede ser cortesía en otra.

stays quiet may come across as thoughtful rather than unfriendly.
teaching.audioText: In some families silence is not rude; a guest who stays quiet may come across as thoughtful rather than unfriendly.

teaching.en: The exchange student did not take offence; her first reaction was to ask a polite question instead of judging her hosts.
teaching.es: La estudiante de intercambio no se ofendió; su primera reacción fue hacer una pregunta educada en lugar de juzgar a sus anfitriones.
teaching.explanationEs: La mejor reacción suele ser preguntar con tacto, no acusar.
segments: The exchange student did not take offence; her first reaction was
to ask a polite question instead of judging her hosts.
teaching.audioText: The exchange student did not take offence; her first reaction was to ask a polite question instead of judging her hosts.

teaching.en: When a custom seems strange, give the benefit of the doubt before you decide that anybody was rude.
teaching.es: Cuando una costumbre parece extraña, concede el beneficio de la duda antes de decidir que alguien fue maleducado.
teaching.explanationEs: Empieza por suponer buena intención y luego pregunta.

prompt.es: Lee el relato: ¿cuál fue el supuesto que hizo Mia sobre la cena?

choices.text: That dinner would be late, as at home.
That her host family wanted her to leave early.
That her dress was too formal for an ordinary family dinner.

feedback.es: Mia cree que se cena tarde, como en su país: ese supuesto oculto explica que llegue a las ocho cuando ya han terminado.

hint.es: Piensa en lo que ella esperaba antes de llegar.

origin.text: Mia, an exchange student, arrived at her host family's house at eight, wearing her best dress, for a dinner that she assumed would start late. The family had already finished, because they always eat at six. Mia went red and apologised three times.

prompt.es: Completa: «Da a los demás el beneficio de la duda.»

feedback.es: Give the benefit of the doubt es la expresión fija para suponer buena intención hasta tener pruebas contrarias.

origin.text: Before you decide that the family was rude, give them the benefit of the ___. They may simply have assumed that you knew their custom.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con su significado.

feedback.es: Son cuatro piezas de cualquier relato de malentendidos: el problema, la reacción, el contexto y la impresión que se da.

hint.es: Piensa en un relato: problema, reacción, lugar e impresión.

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué suponía la estudiante que iba a ocurrir en la casa de acogida?

choices.text: That leaving food on the plate would offend the host mother.
That a student should never accept a second helping.
That a host should decide how much a guest eats.
That a first refusal is polite and will be followed by an offer.

feedback.es: Ella suponía que rechazar es educado y que la oferta se repetiría; la familia tomó el rechazo literalmente. Dos supuestos distintos, no mala educación.

origin.audio: An exchange student from Japan told us that in her country it is polite to refuse a second helping once or twice. In her host family's home, she refused twice and went to bed hungry, because nobody offered a third time. The next morning, her host mother explained that here a refusal is taken at face value. They laughed about it, and since then the family has learned to insist a little, while the student has learned to say yes.

prompt.es: Lee el caso: ¿por qué se sintió avergonzada Sara?

choices.text: Her polite phrase was understood literally.
Her host had not offered her any food.
She had eaten more than the family expected.
Her host thought that she was being rude.

feedback.es: Sara solo quería decir que estaba casi llena y el anfitrión lo entendió al pie de la letra: hubo dos supuestos, no mala educación.

origin.text: When Sara thanked her host by saying that she would not eat anything else, he took her at her word and cleared the plates. Sara, who had meant that she was almost full, felt embarrassed. Nobody was rude; both had simply assumed that the other used words in the same way.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Nadie quiso hacer daño, pero suponían cosas distintas.»

answer.text: Nobody meant any harm, but they assumed different things

feedback.es: Nobody meant any harm separa la intención del resultado; but introduce el contraste con assumed different things.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato: ¿qué supuesto tenía la familia sobre Marta?

choices.text: That she disliked the food that the family usually cooked for guests.
That she was unhappy or shy, since she never opened the fridge.
That she expected the mother to serve her every meal.
That she was used to eating alone in her own room.

feedback.es: Cada lado suponía algo distinto: Marta esperaba que le ofrecieran comida; la familia creyó que era tímida o infeliz por no abrir la nevera.

origin.audio: Last spring, Marta, an exchange student from Chile, stayed with a family in Leeds. On her first evening, the father told her to help herself to anything in the kitchen. Marta, who had been raised to wait until food is offered, thanked him and stayed hungry until breakfast. The family, in turn, noticed that she never opened the fridge and assumed that she was unhappy or shy. Only after a week did the mother say, over tea, that in their house guests are expected to serve themselves, and that asking is not needed. Marta burst out laughing, and so did everyone else. From then on, the fridge became the centre of their conversations.

prompt.es: ¿Qué reacción le conviene más a Tom la próxima vez, según el caso?

choices.text: Tell his manager that the colleague had been rude to him during the meeting.
Stop presenting proposals to colleagues from other countries.
Ask what the next step is before reporting an approval.
Insist until the colleague finally answers yes or no in plain words.

feedback.es: Preguntar con tacto por el siguiente paso evita suponer un sí; acusar, rendirse o forzar una respuesta directa ignora que el colega quiso evitar la vergüenza.

origin.text: Tom's Japanese colleague smiled slightly and said that Tom's proposal was very interesting, then changed the subject. Tom left the meeting pleased and told his manager that the idea had been approved. A week later he learned that the colleague had meant that the proposal could not go ahead. The colleague felt that a direct refusal would have embarrassed them both.

prompt.es: Completa: «Puede dar la impresión de ser tímido.»

feedback.es: Come across as describe la impresión que causa alguien, que puede no coincidir con su intención real.

origin.text: A guest who never speaks during dinner may come ___ as shy, although in his family silence is a sign of respect.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada situación con el supuesto que la explica.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la postura de quien escribe la columna sobre los malentendidos?

choices.text: Travel makes people more open in almost every case.
Bad manners are the main cause of trouble between countries.
Guests should wait patiently and let hosts explain their customs.
Asking questions beats simply being patient.

feedback.es: Considera que la paciencia no basta y propone preguntar antes de juzgar; el origen del problema es suponer que nuestras costumbres son universales.

origin.text: We like to think that travel opens the mind, yet most misunderstandings come from a simple failure to think. We assume that our habits are the normal setting everywhere, and when a host acts differently, we explain it as bad manners. Curiosity, not patience, is the better response: ask first, judge later.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Concede a tu anfitrión el beneficio de la duda.»

answer.text: Give your host the benefit of the doubt

feedback.es: Give + persona + the benefit of the doubt: el anfitrión va antes de la expresión fija.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje: ¿qué quiere aclarar Sara a Marta?

choices.text: That “we will see” was a refusal, not a promise.
That Sunday is the best day for a family dinner.
That Marta should ask before accepting an invitation.
That her family always says no to every invitation.

feedback.es: Sara explica que su «we would see» era un no cortés, reconoce que debió decirlo con claridad y pide que no se haya ofendido.

origin.audio: Hello Marta, it is Sara. I am sorry about last night. When I told you that we would see about Sunday, I did not mean yes. In my family that is a polite no. I should have said so clearly, and I hope that you did not take offence.
